cues.text: Welcome to the Athar Open Agentic Pact, a community proposal from ODA and AIREV.
This guided narration walks you through the pact, its community model, six pillars, governance, impact tiers, and the Athar OS roadmap.
Use the arrows to move at your own pace.
Section one, the Pact.
The Athar Open Agentic Pact is an open commitment between institutions, partners and platforms to learn, build and deploy agentic AI for public benefit.
It is a community proposal from ODA and AI Rev, designed as a community, not a product.
Signatories agree on shared standards, an open plugin approach and measurable real-world outcomes.
Section two, the Community Model.
Every webinar, chapter event and challenge should lead somewhere real, so the model is built around four outcomes for every participant.

Learn agentic AI, build a useful agent through the Builder Journey and Marketplace, deploy it through a named Accountable Institution, and measure a real-world benefit with baseline evidence of time saved, better service, or wider reach.
This is a managed global programme, not a social channel.
A Community Director, country chapter leads and a governance council run it against a published calendar.
Every activity has an owner, a target and a report, so membership means participation in a working system rather than a mailing list.
Discord is the always-on home of the community.
Chapters, cohorts and office hours live in structured channels with clear moderation and escalation.
It is where builders ask questions, showcase agents and find collaborators between events — governed, searchable and open to every member.
Country chapters bring the pact to life locally.
Each chapter adapts the shared curriculum to its language and institutions, hosts events, and connects local builders with government and industry partners.
Wave one starts with the UAE base plus two countries, then scales through the roadmap.
Webinars, bootcamps and institutional academies form the learning ladder.
Webinars introduce agentic AI, bootcamps build working agents in days, and academies embed the practice inside ministries, universities and companies.
Every step issues evidence a learner can carry into the marketplace.
Challenges, showcases and the annual summit turn learning into visible results.
Time-boxed challenges solve real institutional problems, showcases publish validated agents, and the Global Summit reports the year's outcomes to funders and governments in one place.
Weekly office hours and tiered support keep builders unblocked.
Level one answers common questions in the community, level two brings platform engineers, and level three escalates to AIREV specialists.
Institutions on a licence receive committed response times.
The builder journey runs from an idea to a validated agent.
Prototype, evaluate, validate — then publish in the agent marketplace with a disclosed intended use, a named owner and supported languages.
Specialist agents can earn revenue share, sustaining the builders who create them.
The decision in one page.
Approve the two-engine model — institutions and community — appoint the Community Director, select the first anchor institutions, and fund the founding cohort.
Everything else on the roadmap follows from these four decisions.
Section three, six pillars.
Plugins are the connective tissue: one shared plugin standard, so every integration works everywhere.
Reusable skills are built once and shared across the community.
Open where possible, governed where necessary.
Interfaces, curricula and the plugin standard are open; identity, data residency and deployment approvals are governed.
The balance lets institutions adopt with confidence while the community keeps building in the open.
Cross-model interoperability by design.
The pact does not bind any nation or institution to a single model.
Agents, skills and plugins run across leading models, so partners can switch providers, host sovereign models and stay in control of cost and residency.
Universal API licences are managed by Athar, giving members access without duplicated procurement.
Agentic AI for all, not for a few.
The pact is bilingual by design, accessible by requirement, and priced so a school or clinic can start small.
Reach is measured, not assumed — with learners, deployments and benefits reported by country and by institution.
Section four, Pledge and Signing.
Joining the Pact is a simple public commitment.
A signatory chooses its roles, sign, govern, build or learn, and pledges to contribute to at least one of the four participant outcomes.
Signing brings access to the learning pathway, the builder journey, and the plugin standard, together with a commitment to report outcomes through the shared impact tiers.

Section five, Actors and Roles, institutions, partners and platforms building the Athar ecosystem together, ODA and AIREV sign and govern, with AIREV, OnDemand, e& and ai& and Discord building, UNDP, UNICEF, IFRC, WFP and UNHCR sign and learn.
The UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade signs and governs and the United Arab Emirates governs.
Who signs the pact.
Institutions sign to deploy validated agents inside accountable workflows, backed by a licence, a named owner and quarterly reporting.
Signing gives access to the marketplace, the academies and the shared plugin standard.
Every actor has a clear role, sign, govern, build or learn.
Who builds on the pact.
Developers, practitioners and student teams build agents and skills through the marketplace, with office hours, review and revenue share for specialist work.
Builders keep their intellectual property while publishing under the shared standard.
Who learns through the pact.
Public servants, teachers, clinicians, farmers and young people move from foundations to certification.
Year-one targets: ten thousand learners, two thousand five hundred certified and one hundred facilitators — each recorded against a baseline.
Section six, governance and roadmap.
An open steering council sets the shared plugin standard and approves the roadmap.
Decisions, releases, and outcome reports are published, so every member can see how priorities are set and how the platform evolves over time.
Section seven, Impact and Funding.
Three impact tiers, one delivery model, access, ownership, legacy.
A funder can enter at any tier and climb.
Every agreement includes named cohorts and activation targets, independent evaluator baselines, quarterly outcome reports, and open book costs with unspent funds returned.
Universal API licenses, marketplace revenue share and sovereign pilot options fund the model so each partner can choose what fits.
Delivered with candidate partners across the humanitarian, development and technology sectors, shown here for internal review only pending written authorisation.
Funders receive the same open-book reporting as signatories, aligned to the three impact tiers.
Join the pact.
You have seen the agreement, the community model, the six pillars, the actors, the roadmap, the impact tiers and Athar OS.
Now the invitation is yours.
Choose your role: sign, govern, build or learn.
Commit to one real outcome, a learner trained, an agent built, a deployment inside your institution, or a benefit measured.
The founding cohort starts this quarter.
Open the pledge, add your name, and help us build agentic AI that leaves a lasting trace.
This is the Athar Open Agentic Pact.
Join us.
Section eight, Athar OS.
The product tour shows the real screens: the marketplace, the playground, the agent flow builder and the tools and deployment views, captured from the Athar OS wireframes and the launch film.
The roadmap runs now in Q4, 2026, next in 2027 and later in 2028.
Deploy anywhere, own it.
Option A runs software-only on your own hardware, option B is self-hosted in your cloud, option C is fully managed by AIREV.
Sovereign nodes transfer to national ownership after five to seven years, with local operators trained to run them.
Nations empowered.
Lebanon, Access, 1 million Lebanese AI experts at $10 million.
India, ownership, 100 government schools and 10,000 AI PCs at 13.7 million.
Kenya, Legacy, a Kenyan-owned sovereign node at around 33 million transferred to a national entity after five to seven years.
Join the Pact.
You have seen the agreement, the community model, the six pillars, the actors, the roadmap, the impact tiers and Athar OS.
Now the invitation is yours.
Choose your role, sign, govern, build or learn.
Commit to one real outcome.
The founding cohort starts this quarter.
Open the pledge, add your name and help us build a Gentick AI that leaves a lasting trace.
Join us.
